100

103	      payload[0] = "0".charCodeAt(0)

# wterm.dev Integration Research

**1. NPM package name:** `@wterm/dom` (scoped under `@wterm`). A separate `@wterm/react` is available for React. The underlying parser is `@wterm/core` but `@wterm/dom` re-exports what you need.

**2. Import API:**
```js
import { WTerm } from "@wterm/dom";
import "@wterm/dom/css";
```
Note: the class is `WTerm` (not `Terminal` like xterm.js).

**3. WASM init:** Yes — WASM is embedded in the package, but you must `await term.init()` after construction. The constructor takes the DOM element directly, so there's no separate `open()` step.

**4. Terminal class methods:**
| Need | wterm API |
|------|-----------|
| Write bytes | `term.write(data)` — accepts `string` or `Uint8Array` |
| Handle input | `term.onData = (data) => {...}` (property, not `.onData(cb)` like xterm) |
| Resize | `term.resize(cols, rows)` |
| Open/mount | Passed into constructor: `new WTerm(el)` + `await term.init()` |
| Focus | `term.focus()` |
| Dispose | `term.destroy()` (note: NOT `dispose()` like xterm.js) |

**5. CSS:** Yes — `import "@wterm/dom/css"`. Built-in themes applied via `el.classList.add("theme-solarized-dark" | "theme-monokai" | "theme-light")`.

**6. Quickstart (ttyd bridge pattern):**
```js
import { WTerm } from "@wterm/dom";
import "@wterm/dom/css";

const term = new WTerm(document.getElementById("terminal"));
await term.init();

const ws = new WebSocket(ttydUrl, ["tty"]);
ws.binaryType = "arraybuffer";
ws.onmessage = (ev) => {
  const buf = new Uint8Array(ev.data);
  if (buf[0] === 0x30) term.write(buf.subarray(1)); // '0' = output frame
};
term.onData = (data) => {
  const payload = new TextEncoder().encode("0" + data); // ttyd input frame
  ws.send(payload);
};
term.focus();
```

**Caveats vs xterm.js:** `onData` is an assignable property (no disposable returned), cleanup method is `destroy()` not `dispose()`, and mount happens in the constructor rather than via `.open(el)`. Repo: https://github.com/vercel-labs/wterm (Vercel Labs, Zig→WASM).

Sources:
- [wterm.dev](https://wterm.dev/)
- [Get Started](https://wterm.dev/get-started)
- [@wterm/dom README](https://github.com/vercel-labs/wterm/blob/main/packages/@wterm/dom/README.md)
- [vercel-labs/wterm](https://github.com/vercel-labs/wterm)

# @wterm/dom

DOM renderer, input handler, and orchestrator for [wterm](https://github.com/vercel-labs/wterm) — a terminal emulator for the web. No framework required.

Re-exports everything from `@wterm/core`, so this is the only package you need for vanilla JS usage.

## Install

```bash
npm install @wterm/dom
```

## Usage

```html
<div id="terminal"></div>

<script type="module">
  import { WTerm } from "@wterm/dom";
  import "@wterm/dom/css";

  const term = new WTerm(document.getElementById("terminal"));
  await term.init();
</script>
```

The WASM binary is embedded in the package — no extra setup required. To serve it separately instead, pass `wasmUrl`.

## API

### `WTerm`

The main terminal class.

```ts
new WTerm(element: HTMLElement, options?: WTermOptions)
```

**Options:**

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cols` | `number` | `80` | Initial column count |
| `rows` | `number` | `24` | Initial row count |
| `wasmUrl` | `string` | — | Optional URL to serve the WASM binary separately (embedded by default) |
| `autoResize` | `boolean` | `true` | Auto-resize based on container dimensions |
| `cursorBlink` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable cursor blinking animation |
| `debug` | `boolean` | `false` | Enable debug mode. Exposes a `DebugAdapter` on the instance (`wt.debug`) for inspecting escape sequences, cell data, render performance, and unhandled CSI sequences. |
| `onData` | `(data: string) => void` | — | Called when the terminal produces data (user input or host response). When omitted, input is echoed back automatically. |
| `onTitle` | `(title: string) => void` | — | Called when the terminal title changes |
| `onResize` | `(cols: number, rows: number) => void` | — | Called on resize |

**Methods:**

| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `init(): Promise<WTerm>` | Load WASM and start rendering |
| `write(data: string \| Uint8Array)` | Write data to the terminal |
| `resize(cols, rows)` | Resize the terminal grid |
| `focus()` | Focus the terminal element |
| `destroy()` | Clean up event listeners and DOM |

### `WebSocketTransport`

Connect to a PTY backend over WebSocket (re-exported from `@wterm/core`).

```ts
import { WTerm, WebSocketTransport } from "@wterm/dom";

const term = new WTerm(el, { cols: 80, rows: 24 });
await term.init();

const ws = new WebSocketTransport({
  url: "ws://localhost:8080/pty",
  onData: (data) => term.write(data),
});

ws.connect();
term.onData = (data) => ws.send(data);
```

## Themes

Import the stylesheet and apply a theme class to the terminal element:

```js
import "@wterm/dom/css";
```

Built-in themes: `theme-solarized-dark`, `theme-monokai`, `theme-light`. Apply via class name:

```js
element.classList.add("theme-monokai");
```

All colors use CSS custom properties (`--term-fg`, `--term-bg`, `--term-color-0` through `--term-color-15`, etc.) so you can define your own theme with plain CSS.

1	class TerminalController < ApplicationController
2	  layout "terminal", only: :show
3	
4	  allow_unauthenticated_access only: :auth
5	  skip_before_action :require_password_change, only: :auth
6	  skip_forgery_protection only: :open
7	
8	  def open
9	    sandbox = find_sandbox
10	    type    = params[:type].presence_in(%w[tmux shell]) || "tmux"
11	    TerminalManager.new.open(sandbox: sandbox, type: type)
12	    redirect_to terminal_show_path(sandbox, type), status: :see_other
13	  rescue TerminalManager::Error => e
14	    redirect_to root_path, alert: e.message
15	  end
16	
17	  def show
18	    @sandbox = find_sandbox
19	    @emulator = Current.user.terminal_emulator || "xterm"
20	    type = params[:type].presence_in(%w[tmux shell]) || "tmux"
21	
22	    terminal_base = ENV["SANDCASTLE_TERMINAL_URL"].presence
23	    if terminal_base
24	      # SANDCASTLE_TERMINAL_URL is a full URL (e.g. https://dev.sand:8443)
25	      uri = URI.parse(terminal_base)
26	      ws_proto = uri.scheme == "https" ? "wss" : "ws"
27	      @ws_url    = "#{ws_proto}://#{uri.host}:#{uri.port}/terminal/#{@sandbox.id}/#{type}/ws"
28	      @token_url = "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}:#{uri.port}/terminal/#{@sandbox.id}/#{type}/token"
29	    else
30	      proto = request.ssl? ? "wss:" : "ws:"
31	      host  = request.host_with_port
32	      @ws_url    = "#{proto}//#{host}/terminal/#{@sandbox.id}/#{type}/ws"
33	      @token_url = "#{request.protocol}#{host}/terminal/#{@sandbox.id}/#{type}/token"
34	    end
35	  end
36	
37	  def close
38	    sandbox = find_sandbox
39	
40	    TerminalManager.new.close(sandbox: sandbox)
41	    redirect_to root_path, notice: "Terminal closed"
42	  rescue TerminalManager::Error => e
43	    redirect_to root_path, alert: e.message
44	  end
45	
46	  private
47	
48	  def find_sandbox
49	    scope = Current.user.admin? ? Sandbox.active : Current.user.sandboxes.active
50	    scope.find(params[:id])
51	  end
52	
53	  public
54	
55	  # Called by Traefik forwardAuth. Returns 200 to allow, or redirects to
56	  # login (which Traefik passes through to the browser).
57	  def auth
58	    forwarded_uri = request.headers["X-Forwarded-Uri"] || ""
59	    match = forwarded_uri.match(%r{/terminal/(\d+)/(tmux|shell)})
60	    head(:unauthorized) and return unless match
61	
62	    session_record = find_session_by_cookie
63	    unless session_record
64	      proto = request.headers["X-Forwarded-Proto"] || "https"
65	      host  = request.headers["X-Forwarded-Host"] || request.host_with_port
66	      original_url = "#{proto}://#{host}#{forwarded_uri}"
67	      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = original_url
68	      redirect_to new_session_url, allow_other_host: true
69	      return
70	    end
71	
72	    user    = session_record.user
73	    sandbox = Sandbox.active.find_by(id: match[1].to_i)
74	    head(:unauthorized) and return unless sandbox && (sandbox.user_id == user.id || user.admin?)
75	
76	    head :ok
77	  end
78	end

1	import { Controller } from "@hotwired/stimulus"
2	import { Terminal } from "@xterm/xterm"
3	import { FitAddon } from "@xterm/addon-fit"
4	import { WebLinksAddon } from "@xterm/addon-web-links"
5	
6	// Bridges xterm.js terminal with ttyd's WebSocket protocol.
7	// Same protocol as ghostty_terminal_controller but using xterm.js as the renderer.
8	export default class extends Controller {
9	  static values = { wsUrl: String, tokenUrl: String }
10	
11	  async connect() {
12	    this.encoder = new TextEncoder()
13	    this.decoder = new TextDecoder()
14	
15	    this.fitAddon = new FitAddon()
16	
17	    this.terminal = new Terminal({
18	      fontSize: 14,
19	      fontFamily: "Menlo, Monaco, 'Courier New', monospace",
20	      cursorBlink: true,
21	      theme: {
22	        background: "#1a1b26",
23	        foreground: "#a9b1d6",
24	        cursor: "#a9b1d6",
25	      },
26	    })
27	
28	    this.terminal.loadAddon(this.fitAddon)
29	    this.terminal.loadAddon(new WebLinksAddon())
30	    this.terminal.open(this.element)
31	    this.fitAddon.fit()
32	
33	    this.terminal.onData((data) => this.sendInput(data))
34	    this.terminal.onBinary((data) => this.sendBinary(data))
35	    this.terminal.onResize(({ cols, rows }) => this.sendResize(cols, rows))
36	
37	    this.token = await this.fetchToken()
38	    this.connectWebSocket()
39	
40	    this.resizeObserver = new ResizeObserver(() => {
41	      try { this.fitAddon.fit() } catch {}
42	    })
43	    this.resizeObserver.observe(this.element)
44	  }
45	
46	  disconnect() {
47	    this.resizeObserver?.disconnect()
48	    this.socket?.close()
49	    this.terminal?.dispose()
50	  }
51	
52	  async fetchToken() {
53	    try {
54	      const resp = await fetch(this.tokenUrlValue)
55	      if (resp.ok) {
56	        const json = await resp.json()
57	        return json.token
58	      }
59	    } catch (e) {
60	      console.warn("[xterm] token fetch failed:", e)
61	    }
62	    return ""
63	  }
64	
65	  connectWebSocket() {
66	    this.socket = new WebSocket(this.wsUrlValue, ["tty"])
67	    this.socket.binaryType = "arraybuffer"
68	
69	    this.socket.addEventListener("open", () => {
70	      const msg = JSON.stringify({
71	        AuthToken: this.token,
72	        columns: this.terminal.cols,
73	        rows: this.terminal.rows,
74	      })
75	      this.socket.send(this.encoder.encode(msg))
76	      this.terminal.focus()
77	    })
78	
79	    this.socket.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
80	      const rawData = event.data
81	      const cmd = String.fromCharCode(new Uint8Array(rawData)[0])
82	      const data = rawData.slice(1)
83	
84	      switch (cmd) {
85	        case "0": // OUTPUT
86	          this.terminal.write(new Uint8Array(data))
87	          break
88	        case "1": // SET_WINDOW_TITLE
89	          document.title = this.decoder.decode(data) + " — Sandcastle"
90	          break
91	        case "2": // SET_PREFERENCES (ignored)
92	          break
93	      }
94	    })
95	
96	    this.socket.addEventListener("close", (event) => {
97	      if (event.code !== 1000) {
98	        console.log("[xterm] connection lost, reconnecting...")
99	        setTimeout(() => this.connectWebSocket(), 2000)
100	      }
101	    })
102	  }
103	
104	  sendInput(data) {
105	    if (this.socket?.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return
106	    const payload = new Uint8Array(data.length * 3 + 1)
107	    payload[0] = "0".charCodeAt(0)
108	    const stats = this.encoder.encodeInto(data, payload.subarray(1))
109	    this.socket.send(payload.subarray(0, stats.written + 1))
110	  }
111	
112	  sendBinary(data) {
113	    if (this.socket?.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return
114	    const bytes = new Uint8Array(data.length + 1)
115	    bytes[0] = "0".charCodeAt(0)
116	    for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) bytes[i + 1] = data.charCodeAt(i) & 255
117	    this.socket.send(bytes)
118	  }
119	
120	  sendResize(cols, rows) {
121	    if (this.socket?.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return
122	    const msg = JSON.stringify({ columns: cols, rows: rows })
123	    this.socket.send(this.encoder.encode("1" + msg))
124	  }
125	}
126

{
  "file_path": "/Users/thies/Projects/GitHub/Sandcastle/app/javascript/controllers/wterm_terminal_controller.js",
  "content": "import { Controller } from \"@hotwired/stimulus\"\nimport { WTerm } from \"@wterm/dom\"\n\n// Bridges @wterm/dom terminal with ttyd's WebSocket protocol.\n// Same protocol as ghostty/xterm controllers but using wterm.dev as the renderer.\nexport default class extends Controller {\n  static values = { wsUrl: String, tokenUrl: String }\n\n  async connect() {\n    this.encoder = new TextEncoder()\n    this.decoder = new TextDecoder()\n\n    this.terminal = new WTerm(this.element, {\n      cols: 80,\n      rows: 24,\n      autoResize: true,\n      cursorBlink: true,\n      onData: (data) => this.sendInput(data),\n      onResize: (cols, rows) => this.sendResize(cols, rows),\n      onTitle: (title) => { document.title = title + \" — Sandcastle\" },\n    })\n\n    await this.terminal.init()\n\n    this.token = await this.fetchToken()\n    this.connectWebSocket()\n  }\n\n  disconnect() {\n    this.socket?.close()\n    this.terminal?.destroy()\n  }\n\n  async fetchToken() {\n    try {\n      const resp = await fetch(this.tokenUrlValue)\n      if (resp.ok) {\n        const json = await resp.json()\n        return json.token\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      console.warn(\"[wterm] token fetch failed:\", e)\n    }\n    return \"\"\n  }\n\n  connectWebSocket() {\n    this.socket = new WebSocket(this.wsUrlValue, [\"tty\"])\n    this.socket.binaryType = \"arraybuffer\"\n\n    this.socket.addEventListener(\"open\", () => {\n      const msg = JSON.stringify({\n        AuthToken: this.token,\n        columns: this.terminal.cols || 80,\n        rows: this.terminal.rows || 24,\n      })\n      this.socket.send(this.encoder.encode(msg))\n      this.terminal.focus()\n    })\n\n    this.socket.addEventListener(\"message\", (event) => {\n      const rawData = event.data\n      const cmd = String.fromCharCode(new Uint8Array(rawData)[0])\n      const data = rawData.slice(1)\n\n      switch (cmd) {\n        case \"0\": // OUTPUT\n          this.terminal.write(new Uint8Array(data))\n          break\n        case \"1\": // SET_WINDOW_TITLE\n          document.title = this.decoder.decode(data) + \" — Sandcastle\"\n          break\n        case \"2\": // SET_PREFERENCES (ignored — we use our own theme)\n          break\n      }\n    })\n\n    this.socket.addEventListener(\"close\", (event) => {\n      if (event.code !== 1000) {\n        console.log(\"[wterm] connection lost, reconnecting...\")\n        setTimeout(() => this.connectWebSocket(), 2000)\n      }\n    })\n  }\n\n  sendInput(data) {\n    if (this.socket?.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return\n\n    if (typeof data === \"string\") {\n      const payload = new Uint8Array(data.length * 3 + 1)\n      payload[0] = \"0\".charCodeAt(0)\n      const stats = this.encoder.encodeInto(data, payload.subarray(1))\n      this.socket.send(payload.subarray(0, stats.written + 1))\n    } else {\n      const payload = new Uint8Array(data.length + 1)\n      payload[0] = \"0\".charCodeAt(0)\n      payload.set(data, 1)\n      this.socket.send(payload)\n    }\n  }\n\n  sendResize(cols, rows) {\n    if (this.socket?.readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN) return\n    const msg = JSON.stringify({ columns: cols, rows: rows })\n    this.socket.send(this.encoder.encode(\"1\" + msg))\n  }\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Added wterm.dev (`@wterm/dom` 0.1.9, WASM bundled via jsdelivr `+esm`) as a third emulator choice alongside xterm.js and Ghostty Web.

**Files changed:**
- `config/importmap.rb:9` — pin `@wterm/dom` to jsdelivr `+esm` (transitively pulls `@wterm/core` with inlined WASM)
- `app/javascript/controllers/wterm_terminal_controller.js` — new Stimulus controller bridging ttyd protocol to `WTerm` (uses `onData/onResize/onTitle` constructor callbacks, `init()`, `destroy()`)
- `app/assets/stylesheets/wterm.css` — minified `@wterm/dom` theme; `WTerm` adds class `wterm` to its element automatically
- `app/views/terminal/show.html.erb` — third branch selecting `wterm-terminal` controller
- `app/views/layouts/terminal.html.erb` — load `wterm.css` when emulator is `wterm`
- `app/views/settings/show.html.erb:161` — added `["wterm", "wterm"]` to the dropdown with description/link
- `app/models/user.rb:30` — extended inclusion list to `%w[ghostty xterm wterm]`
- `app/views/pages/guide.html.erb` — note the three renderer options in the Web Terminal section

No migration needed (column already `string default: "xterm"`). Tests couldn't run locally (no Postgres — use `mise run deploy:dev`), but rubocop on the Ruby files is clean.

> AGENT

Found it. The stack is fine — it's a host-routing issue.

- Traefik only has a router for `Host(`dev.sand`)` (from `DEV_HOST=dev.sand` in `.env`). Any other Host header → 404.
- Your `/etc/hosts` points `dev.sand` at **`100.106.185.92`** (sandman, your Tailscale IP), not `127.0.0.1`. So typing `dev.sand` sends you to the production box, and `127.0.0.1:8080` doesn't match any router locally.

Two ways to fix for local dev:

**A. Point `dev.sand` at localhost** — edit `/etc/hosts`:
```
127.0.0.1  dev.sand
```
(and comment out / remove the `100.106.185.92  dev.sand` line), then visit `http://dev.sand:8080`.

**B. Switch the local stack to `localhost`** — edit `.env`:
```
DEV_HOST=localhost
```
then `mise run deploy:dev:down && mise run deploy:dev`. Then `http://localhost:8080` works.

Which do you want? I'd suggest **A** since it matches the existing `SANDCASTLE_TERMINAL_URL` assumptions; the tradeoff is you temporarily can't reach production via `dev.sand` (use `sandman` alias instead).

> AGENT

Found the root cause in `sandcastle-worker` logs — it's **not** related to the wterm change:

```
Docker::Error::NotFoundError:
  "no matching manifest for linux/arm64/v8 in the manifest list entries:
   no match for platform in manifest: not found"

app/services/sandbox_manager.rb:119: ensure_image
app/jobs/sandbox_provision_job.rb:16
```

The worker is trying to pull `ghcr.io/thieso2/sandcastle-sandbox:latest`, and that image on GHCR has no **linux/arm64** manifest — only amd64. Your Mac is Apple Silicon, so Docker asks for arm64 and the pull fails. The sandbox row gets created in the DB (status `pending`) and then the provision job explodes.

The web POST itself succeeded (302 + `Sandbox Create INSERT`). The unrelated `NameError: undefined local variable or method 'tailscale_path'` on line 55 of `app/views/layouts/admin.html.erb` is a separate bug hit when you view the Solid Errors admin page — worth a ticket but not blocking this.

Two options to get past the arm64 block:

**A. Build the sandbox image locally for arm64:**
```
docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 \
  -t ghcr.io/thieso2/sandcastle-sandbox:latest --load \
  images/sandbox
```
Then it's in your local daemon's cache and `Docker::Image.create` will find it without pulling.

**B. Run the web/worker containers under amd64 emulation** — slower, and you'd have to rebuild the dev image.

Want me to run **A**? It takes a few minutes (and the Dockerfile needs the base image to have arm64 too, which I should check first). Or do you want to push a multi-arch tag to GHCR from your release pipeline instead?

  def ensure_image(image)

    # Create BTRFS subvolume for user directory if on BTRFS

    # Ensure user base directory is writable (may be root-owned from previous install)
    ensure_dir("#{DATA_DIR}/users/#{user.name}")

> AGENT

Quick check before committing to a 15–30 min rebuild: the **base** image (`sandcastle-sandbox-base:latest`, which your Dockerfile `FROM`s) is also amd64-only. So option A really means rebuilding *both* base and the thin layer for arm64. Base installs Chromium/Docker/tmux/etc. — doable (Dockerfile handles arm64 correctly at line 46/128/137), but slow.

There's a **faster dev path** that gets sandbox creation working in ~1 minute: pull the existing amd64 image explicitly, let `Docker::Image.get` find it locally, and run the sandbox under Rosetta emulation. Sandcastle's `ensure_image` (`app/services/sandbox_manager.rb:117`) tries `Docker::Image.get` first and only pulls on miss — so pre-staging the amd64 image fixes creation without changing code or rebuilding anything.

Which do you want?
- **Fast path** (recommended for wterm UI verification): I run `docker pull --platform linux/amd64 ghcr.io/thieso2/sandcastle-sandbox:latest` and retry.
- **True arm64 build**: I run `docker buildx build --platform linux/arm64 …` for both base and final images. Longer, but you get native performance on all subsequent runs.

162	# StrictModes no: the home dir is bind-mounted from the host.  Sysbox user-

171	    && echo "PasswordAuthentication no" >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-sandcastle.conf \

1	# Thin layer on top of the pre-built base image.
2	# Changes here (entrypoint, config, scripts) build in seconds.
3	# To rebuild the base: trigger the "Rebuild Sandbox Base Image" workflow
4	# or change files in images/sandbox/base/.
5	FROM ghcr.io/thieso2/sandcastle-sandbox-base:latest
6	
7	ARG SANDCASTLE_VERSION=dev
8	
9	# Always pull latest security patches and package updates.
10	# CACHE_DATE is set at build time to bust the layer cache on demand.
11	#
12	# Hold Docker-stack packages before upgrading: the base image pins
13	# containerd.io=1.7.27-1 (see Dockerfile.base for rationale — containerd.io ≥ 2.x
14	# breaks sysbox-runc, nestybox/sysbox#958). Without the hold, `apt-get upgrade`
15	# installs containerd.io 2.x, which also replaces /usr/bin/runc with a newer
16	# runc (1.3.3+) whose CVE-2025-52881 fix rejects sysbox's FUSE-backed procfs
17	# with "unsafe procfs detected" and breaks docker-in-docker inside sandboxes.
18	# Re-install the pinned runc afterwards as belt-and-suspenders in case an
19	# older base image (built before the apt-mark hold was added) is used.
20	ARG CACHE_DATE=0
21	RUN apt-mark hold docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin \
22	    && for i in 1 2 3; do apt-get update && break || sleep 5; done \
23	    && apt-get upgrade -y \
24	    && RUNC_VERSION="v1.1.15" \
25	    && ARCH=$(dpkg --print-architecture) \
26	    && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/download/${RUNC_VERSION}/runc.${ARCH}" \
27	       -o /usr/bin/runc \
28	    && chmod +x /usr/bin/runc \
29	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
30	
31	# Bake version into the image
32	RUN echo "${SANDCASTLE_VERSION}" > /etc/sandcastle-version
33	
34	# ssh-agent-switcher — daemon that proxies SSH agent requests to the most
35	# recent valid forwarded agent socket, surviving tmux detach/reattach.
36	ARG TARGETARCH
37	RUN SAS_VERSION="v1.0.1.1-tc" \
38	    && SAS_ARCH=$([ "$TARGETARCH" = "arm64" ] && echo "aarch64" || echo "x86_64") \
39	    && curl -fsSL "https://github.com/thieso2/ssh-agent-switcher/releases/download/${SAS_VERSION}/ssh-agent-switcher-${SAS_ARCH}-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz" \
40	       | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin ssh-agent-switcher \
41	    && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/ssh-agent-switcher
42	
43	# SSH agent forwarding: prefer ssh-agent-switcher daemon socket, fall back
44	# to the stable symlink maintained by sc-tmux.
45	RUN printf '# ssh-agent-switcher daemon socket or symlink fallback\nif [ -S "/tmp/ssh-agent.${USER}" ]; then\n    export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="/tmp/ssh-agent.${USER}"\nelif [ -S "$HOME/.ssh/agent_sock" ]; then\n    export SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.ssh/agent_sock"\nfi\n' \
46	       > /etc/profile.d/ssh-agent.sh
47	
48	COPY entrypoint.sh /entrypoint.sh
49	COPY docker-restart.sh /usr/local/bin/docker-restart
50	COPY sc-tmux.sh /usr/local/bin/sc-tmux
51	RUN chmod +x /entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/docker-restart /usr/local/bin/sc-tmux
52	
53	COPY startchrome.sh /usr/local/bin/google-chrome
54	RUN chmod +x /usr/local/bin/google-chrome \
55	    && ln -sf /usr/local/bin/google-chrome /usr/local/bin/startchrome
56	
57	COPY tmux.conf /etc/tmux.conf
58	COPY gitconfig /etc/gitconfig
59	
60	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/thieso2/sandcastle"
61	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="Sandcastle sandbox image — Ubuntu 25.10 with Docker-in-Docker, SSH, and dev tools"
62	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses="MIT"
63	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="${SANDCASTLE_VERSION}"
64	
65	EXPOSE 22 5900 6080 7681 7682
66	EXPOSE 60000-61000/udp
67	
68	ENTRYPOINT ["/entrypoint.sh"]
69

> AGENT

Both images built for arm64. Go ahead and create a sandbox via the UI — it should now work. (Your previous `cosmic-shark` is stuck in pending; you can destroy it or retry it. If you want me to clean it up via Rails console, say so.)

Note: I used a small workaround during the thin-layer build. The canonical `images/sandbox/Dockerfile` does `apt-get upgrade -y` without `--allow-downgrades`; on arm64 that fails because the base image pulls Chromium from Debian testing (pinned for arm64 only) and some Debian packages are older than Ubuntu 25.10's. I built from a temporary `Dockerfile.dev` with `--allow-downgrades` added — I did **not** commit that change. If you want this fixed properly upstream so CI can multi-arch build, the one-line change in `images/sandbox/Dockerfile:23` is `apt-get upgrade -y --allow-downgrades`. Say the word and I'll make it a real edit.

> AGENT

Found it — **the terminal only routes over HTTPS**, but you're browsing via HTTP.

Traefik's dynamic config for the terminal (written by `app/services/terminal_manager.rb:76,84`) hardcodes `entryPoints: [websecure]`. The *Rails* router is registered on both `web` and `websecure`, so the dashboard works on `:8080`. But terminal paths only listen on `:8443`:

```
$ curl -I -H "Host: dev.sand" http://127.0.0.1:8080/terminal/2/tmux/    → 404
$ curl -kI https://dev.sand:8443/terminal/2/tmux/                        → 302 (login)
```

Ttyd is running fine inside `thies-dark-cobra` on ports 7681 (tmux) and 7682 (shell), so the backend is healthy — it's just not reachable over plain HTTP locally.

**Two ways forward:**

**A. Switch to HTTPS for local dev** (1-line change, no code): open `https://dev.sand:8443/` in the browser. The cert is self-signed — accept the warning. The dashboard, WebSocket, and wterm will all work.

**B. Patch TerminalManager to register both entrypoints** — add `"web"` to the hardcoded `entryPoints` arrays at `app/services/terminal_manager.rb:76` and `:84`. Safe because prod already serves both (Rails router does), and Traefik typically does HTTP→HTTPS redirect at a higher level in prod.

I'd go with **A** for now since it mirrors the prod browsing experience. Want me to do **B** as a real fix instead?

> AGENT

Root cause confirmed — no code change needed. Here's the chain:

1. Dev compose sets `SANDCASTLE_TERMINAL_URL=https://dev.sand:8443` (compose file line 138). `terminal_controller.rb:27` uses that, so the page hard-codes the WebSocket URL as **`wss://dev.sand:8443/terminal/2/tmux/ws`** regardless of what host/port you're currently browsing on.
2. The Traefik terminal router only listens on `websecure` (the 8443 TLS entrypoint), which matches (1).
3. Your browser is at `http://dev.sand:8080`. When wterm.js opens `wss://dev.sand:8443/...`, it runs into the **self-signed cert** that the browser hasn't trusted yet → the WS handshake fails → wterm reconnect-loops → you see `/terminal/auth` polled every ~5s in the Rails log.

**Fix:** browse the whole app over HTTPS so the cert gets trusted.

1. Open `https://dev.sand:8443/` in the browser.
2. Click through the self-signed cert warning (Advanced → Proceed).
3. Log in, open a sandbox's tmux/shell terminal. wterm should connect.

(Alternatively, permanently trust the dev cert in Keychain to avoid the warning — but clicking through once per browser profile is enough.)

Try it and tell me if the terminal still misbehaves — at that point I'd suspect something in the wterm integration itself, and I'll turn to the browser console for the real error.
